E1_API_TIMEOUT_OR_NET.question: Was Puerta del Sol more important in the 16th century or in the 20th century?

options.B: There is not enough information to determine its importance in either the 16th or 20th century.
options.C: It was equally important in both the 16th and 20th centuries.

evidence: The importance of the Puerta del Sol in the sixteenth century was scarce compared to other areas of Madrid, being more relevant the Plaza del Salvador (predecessor of the Plaza de la Villa), the Puerta de Guadalajara, and especially the Plaza Mayor,[1] as shown in the chronicles of the time.

The Puerta del Sol gained prominence in 1906, as it was the year of royal weddings: in January the Infanta Maria Teresa married her first cousin Ferdinand of Bavaria. The news of the engagement of Alfonso XIII to Princess Victoria Eugenia of Battenberg (granddaughter of Queen Victoria of England), who in Spain would be known by her first two names: Victoria Eugenia, also reached Madrid.
